simple.meaning: מַעֲנֶה (maʻăneh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a reply (favorable or contradictory).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 8 times in Job, Proverbs, Micah, beginning at Job 32:3. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲנֶה (H4617) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מַעֲנֶה (maʻăneh) / H4617 is traced through Job 32:3, Job 32:5, Proverbs 15:1, Proverbs 15:23 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

timeline.evidenceText: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.
A gentle answer turns away wrath,
Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth.
The plans of the heart belong to man,
Yahweh has made everything for its own end—
A servant can’t be corrected by words.

definitions.full: H4617. maaneh מַעֲנֶה noun masculine Prov 15:1 answer, response ; — absolute רַֿךְ׳מ 15:1 a Gentle answer ; construct מִּיו מַעֲנִה 15:23 , compare ׳מ לָשׁוֺן 16:1 (i.e. ability to answer); ׳מ אֱלֹהִים Micah 3:7 i.e. response for guidance; absolute also Prov 29:19 response = obedience; Job 32:3 , 5 reply , refutation; suffix לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ 16:4 +? answers (see Toy).
